feeds.title: The Big Picture
feeds.description: Articles on active management, asset allocation, bailouts, data analyses, credit, currency, inflation, employment , economy, digital media and more. The Big Picture is written by Barry L. Ritholtz. He is co-founder, chairman, and chief investment officer of Ritholtz Wealth Management LLC. His career focus has been on how the intersection of behavioral economics and data affects investors.

feeds.title: William Mitchell Blog
feeds.description: Bill Mitchell is a Professor of Economics and Director of the Centre of Full Employment and Equity (CofFEE), at the University of Newcastle, NSW, Australia. His blog is about Modern Monetary Theory with importance to macroeconomic reality. The blog provides information about macroeconomic research, teaching, and advocacy!

feeds.title: Eye On Housing » Macroeconomics
feeds.description: National Association of Home Builders Discusses Economics and Housing Policy. It provides the latest housing forecasts, market trends, in-depth economic analysis, and archival data relating to the housing industry. The highly anticipated forecasting and analysis are provided by NAHB's Economics Group.

feeds.title: Confessions of a Supply-Side Liberal
feeds.description: Confessions of a Supply-Side Liberal was created by Miles Kimball, a Professor at the University of Michigan. His core topics apply supply side solutions to macroeconomic issues and monetary policy. His arguments are well written and thoroughly researched.

feeds.title: Atlanta Fed » Macroblog
feeds.description: The Atlanta Fed's macroblog provides commentary on economic topics including monetary policy, macroeconomic developments, financial issues and Southeast regional trends.

feeds.title: The Slack Wire
feeds.description: Josh Mason, an Assistant Professor of Economics at City University of New York, blogs at The Slack Wire. This economics blog primarily revolves around macroeconomics issues and economic history, which Josh captures extremely well. He does an excellent job of analyzing economic news.

feeds.title: EconoSpeak
feeds.description: The Econospeak blog is a multi-author blog. Self-described as 'annals of the economically incorrect', this frequently updated blog analyzes daily news from an economic perspective, but requires a strong economics background.

feeds.title: The Economic Fractalist Blog
feeds.description: Non-Stochastic Saturation Macroeconomics. Welcome to the small alcove for the advancement of cause and effect saturation macroeconomics. This site pursues the hypothesis that the nature of market valuations and economic cycles is both causal and quantitatively decipherable.

feeds.title: The Grumpy Economist
feeds.description: News, views, and commentary from a free market point of view. I moved from Blogger to Substack in December 2023. For previous posts back to 2011 see my Blogger page at https://johnhcochrane.blogspot.com

feeds.title: VoxDev » Macroeconomics & Growth
feeds.description: VoxDev's Macroeconomics & Growth section features research-based insights and policy discussions on economic development, focusing on growth dynamics, fiscal policy, and structural transformation in developing countries.

feeds.title: MishTalk
feeds.description: This highly praised global economics blog is written by Mike 'Mish' Shedlock, an investment advisor. Mike provides profound comments on macroeconomic trends around the world, which makes this a must read blog.

feeds.title: Stay-At-Home Macro
feeds.description: My goal is to bring the best economic policy and macroeconomics to you. I cover a wide range of topics from inflation to jobs to Child Tax Credits and all things Fed.

feeds.title: In the Long Run
feeds.description: Covers articles about longer term macroeconomic commentary and guidance for financial market investors by Colin Lloyd, who hopes to provide some new insights and provoke debate.

feeds.title: long and variable
feeds.description: Long and Variable is a blog on macroeconomics and public policy. Authored by Professor Tony Yates (University of Birmingham), this blog is quite detailed and knowledgeable about global monetary policy.

feeds.title: Macro and Other Market Musings
feeds.description: Blog by David Beckworth, an associate Professor of Economics at Western Kentucky University, has recently launched an awesome podcast that features well-known economists, many of whom are featured on this list. David's blog highlights is a great place to start to learn about specific economic events.

feeds.title: owenzidar
feeds.description: Oweznzidar is the personal blog of Owen Zidar, an Assistant Professor of Economics at the University of Chicago. Like his field of research, he often blogs about fiscal policy issues and the macroeconomic impact of tax policies.

feeds.title: The Aleph Blog » Macroeconomics
feeds.description: Blog by David Merkel. Helping Institutions and Ordinary People Invest Better by Focusing on Risk Control. My goal is teaching investors about better investing through risk control, and tying all of the markets into a coherent whole.

feeds.title: Economist's View
feeds.description: Mark Thoma, a Professor of Economics at the University of Oregon, writes about macroeconomics on the Economist's View. He posts a daily round-up of interesting blogs links, while sometimes writing his own detailed analysis in longer posts.

feeds.title: Brad DeLong
feeds.description: J. Bradford DeLong was one of the first economics bloggers and his continues to reflect that with a large number of links. DeLong is a Professor of Economics at U.C. Berkeley. His well thought out insights on macroeconomic issues makes this a must-read blog.

feeds.title: Mainly Macro
feeds.description: Comments on macroeconomic issues. Simon Wren-Lewis is Emeritus Professor of Economics and Fellow of Merton College, University of Oxford. His excellent writing style and explanation appeals to economists and non-economists.

feeds.title: Ekonamik
feeds.description: Ekonamik brings essential information about macroeconomics and their effects on the market carefully selected by our editors and inspired by asset management.

feeds.title: Behavioral Macro
feeds.description: Mark Dow's microblog, analyzing global macroeconomic and market issues, often through the prism of our cognitive shortcomings.
